classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that a base greater than one gives exponential growth and select the increasing curved graph with a positive y-intercept.

spec.description: Rising straight line from the axes' intersection, with an upper arrowhead. Positive axes only; no grid or ticks.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative positive-gradient linear graph through the origin; no numerical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied option, visible in the student edition.

spec.description: Positive decreasing concave-up curve, steep near the vertical axis and flattening towards the horizontal axis, with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative decreasing curve; no equation, numerical scale or separately drawn asymptote is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied option, visible in the student edition.

spec.description: Descending straight segment joining a positive vertical intercept to a positive horizontal intercept, without curve arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative negative-gradient linear graph; intercept values are unspecified.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied option, visible in the student edition.

spec.description: Increasing concave-up curve beginning at a positive vertical intercept and ending in an upper-right arrowhead.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative exponential growth graph; the source provides no numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied option, visible in the student edition.

answer.worked: Since the base $3>1$, $y=3^x$ is an exponential growth curve. It increases from a positive $y$-intercept, as shown in D. Correct answer: D.
